header: 1. Overview & Agro-Climatic Requirements
content:
[1. Overview & Agro-Climatic Requirements]
- **Institution**: ICAR - Central Institute for Cotton Research (CICR) & UAS Dharwad (Agricultural Research Station Dharwad/Siruguppa).
- **Key Karnataka Hybrids & Varieties**: DCH-32, Bunny Bt, RCH-2 Bt, Mallika Bt, Sahana, Jayadhar (desi cotton for rainfed northern black soils).
- **Soil & pH**: Deep black cotton soils (vertisols) or fertile sandy loams with excellent drainage. pH 6.5 to 8.5. Tolerates mild salinity.
- **Climate & Temperature**: Warm climate with abundant sunshine. Minimum temperature for germination 16°C; optimal vegetative growth 21°C - 30°C. Water requirement 700-1200 mm.
- **Fertilizer Dose**: Irrigated Bt cotton: 150:75:75 kg N:P2O5:K2O per ha. Split nitrogen: 25% basal, 25% square initiation (35 DAS), 25% flowering (60 DAS), 25% boll development (80 DAS). Spray 1% Magnesium Sulphate + 1% 19:19:19 to prevent leaf reddening.

header: A. Bacterial Blight / Black Arm (Xanthomonas citri pv. malvacearum)
content:
[A. Bacterial Blight / Black Arm (Xanthomonas citri pv. malvacearum)]
- **Symptoms**:
  - Angular leaf spot: Small, angular, dark green water-soaked spots delimited by leaf veinlets.
  - Black arm: Black elongated cankers on petioles and stems, causing branch girdling and breakage.
  - Boll rot: Round, water-soaked black spots on bolls leading to internal lint discoloration.
- **Favorable Weather**: High humidity (>85%), temperatures 28°C - 35°C, windy rainstorms.
- **Management**:
  - Delint acid-delinted seeds with concentrated H2SO4 (100 ml/kg seed) followed by seed treatment with Streptocycline @ 0.1 g/kg.
  - Spray Copper Oxychloride 50% WP @ 2.5 g/L mixed with Streptocycline @ 0.1 g/L (1 g in 10 L water) at 15-day intervals upon first appearance of angular spots.

header: B. Alternaria Leaf Spot (Alternaria macrospora)
content:
[B. Alternaria Leaf Spot (Alternaria macrospora)]
- **Symptoms**: Brown, circular spots with concentric rings on leaves. As spots coalesce, center dries, cracks, and falls out creating a "shot-hole" effect. Severe infection triggers heavy premature defoliation.
- **Management**:
  - Balanced nutrition: Avoid potassium deficiency which predisposes cotton to Alternaria.
  - Foliar spray: Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5 g/L or Propiconazole 25% EC @ 1.0 ml/L or Kresoxim-methyl 44.3% SC @ 1.0 ml/L.

header: C. Cotton Sucking Pest Complex (Thrips, Jassids, Aphids, Whiteflies)
content:
[C. Cotton Sucking Pest Complex (Thrips, Jassids, Aphids, Whiteflies)]
- **Symptoms**:
  - Jassids / Leafhoppers (Amrasca biguttula): Yellowing and downward curling of leaf margins ("hopper burn").
  - Thrips: Silvery patches on lower leaf surface, curling upward of leaf margins.
  - Whiteflies (Bemisia tabaci): Chlorosis, honeydew excretion causing sooty mold, vector for Cotton Leaf Curl Virus (CLCuV).
- **Integrated Management**:
  - Seed treatment with Imidacloprid 70% WS @ 5 g/kg seed.
  - Install yellow and blue sticky traps @ 15-20 traps/acre.
  - Encourage natural predators: Ladybird beetles, Chrysoperla.
  - Chemical spray (Economic Threshold Level ETL reached): Flonicamid 50% WG @ 0.3 g/L or Diafenthiuron 50% WP @ 1.0 g/L or Dinotefuran 20% SG @ 0.4 g/L.

header: 1. Agro-Climatic Requirements & Overview
content:
[1. Agro-Climatic Requirements & Overview]
- **Institutions**: ICAR - Indian Institute of Horticultural Research (IIHR), Bengaluru & University of Agricultural Sciences (UAS), Dharwad.
- **Recommended Commercial Cultivars**: Arka Meghana, Arka Harita, Arka Suphal, Byadagi Kaddi, Byadagi Dabbi (Karnataka GI Tag).
- **Soil & Climate**: Well-drained black soil or rich sandy loam. Optimum soil pH 6.2 to 7.0. Optimum temperature 20°C to 30°C. Heavy rainfall during flowering causes severe flower drop and anthracnose fruit rot.

header: A. Chilli Anthracnose / Fruit Rot / Die-Back (Colletotrichum capsici)
content:
[A. Chilli Anthracnose / Fruit Rot / Die-Back (Colletotrichum capsici)]
- **Primary Source**: ICAR-IIHR Technical Bulletin on Solanaceous Vegetable Protection.
- **Symptoms**:
  - Foliar Die-back: Drying of twigs from tip downward, twigs turn white or greyish with black dot-like acervuli.
  - Fruit Rot: Circular, sunken, water-soaked dark lesions on ripe red fruits with concentric rings of salmon-pink/black fruiting bodies.
- **Cultural & Sanitation**:
  - Seed treatment with *Trichoderma harzianum* or *T. viride* @ 10 g/kg seed.
  - Collect and burn infected twigs and mummified fruits. Avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation during fruiting.
- **Organic & Biological Control**:
  - Spray *Pseudomonas fluorescens* (IIHR formulation) @ 5 g/L or cold-pressed Neem Oil (10,000 ppm) @ 3 ml/L at flowering onset.
- **Chemical Control (CIBRC Approved Dosages)**:
  - Preventive: Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5 g/L or Copper Oxychloride 50% WP @ 2.5 g/L.
  - Curative / High Infection: Azoxystrobin 23% SC @ 1.0 ml/L, or Tebuconazole 50% + Trifloxystrobin 25% WG (Nativo) @ 0.6 g/L, or Difenoconazole 25% EC @ 0.5 ml/L.
  - Spray volume: 500 L/ha. Wait period (PHI): 5-7 days before harvest.

header: B. Chilli Leaf Curl Disease / Murda Complex (Thrips & Mites Vector Complex)
content:
[B. Chilli Leaf Curl Disease / Murda Complex (Thrips & Mites Vector Complex)]
- **Primary Source**: UAS Dharwad Raitha Mitra Extension Guide.
- **Symptoms**:
  - Upward curling of leaf margins with elongation into boat-like shape caused by Scirtothrips dorsalis (Chilli Thrips).
  - Downward curling of leaf margins with inverted boat shape, thickened leathery leaves caused by Polyphagotarsonemus latus (Yellow Mite).
  - Severe stunting, rosette appearance, flower drop, and malformed small fruits.
- **Vector Integrated Management**:
  - Install blue sticky traps @ 25 traps/acre for thrips and yellow sticky traps for whiteflies.
  - Intercrop with 2-3 border rows of maize or sorghum to impede insect vector drift.
  - For Thrips: Spray Fipronil 5% SC @ 1.5 ml/L or Spinetoram 11.7% SC @ 0.9 ml/L.
  - For Yellow Mites: Spray Spiromesifen 22.9% SC @ 1.0 ml/L or Diafenthiuron 50% WP @ 1.2 g/L. Alternate with Neem seed extract 5%.

header: C. Bacterial Leaf Spot (Xanthomonas campestris pv. vesicatoria)
content:
[C. Bacterial Leaf Spot (Xanthomonas campestris pv. vesicatoria)]
- **Symptoms**: Small, dark brown water-soaked circular lesions on leaves, often surrounded by yellow halos. Lesions coalesce causing severe blighting and premature defoliation.
- **Management**:
  - Spray Streptocycline (90:10 Streptomycin + Tetracycline) @ 0.1 g/L (1 g in 10 L water) mixed with Copper Oxychloride 50% WP @ 2.5 g/L at 10-12 day intervals.

header: 1. Overview & Crop Ecology
content:
[1. Overview & Crop Ecology]
- **Institutions**: ICAR - Central Institute for Cotton Research (CICR), Nagpur & UAS Dharwad (Agricultural Research Station, Dharwad).
- **Major Cotton Tracts in Karnataka**: Dharwad, Belagavi, Haveri, Ballari, Raichur, Kalaburagi.
- **Optimum Soil**: Deep black cotton soils (Vertisols) with good moisture retention and pH 6.5 - 8.0.

header: A. Bacterial Blight / Angular Leaf Spot / Blackarm (Xanthomonas citri pv. malvacearum)
content:
[A. Bacterial Blight / Angular Leaf Spot / Blackarm (Xanthomonas citri pv. malvacearum)]
- **Primary Source**: ICAR-CICR Disease Identification and Control Manual.
- **Symptoms**:
  - Angular, water-soaked translucent lesions bounded by leaf veins on foliage. Lesions turn reddish-brown to dark black.
  - Blackarm phase: Deep black elongated lesions on stems and branches causing girdling and breaking of fruiting branches.
  - Boll rot: Dark, sunken circular spots on developing bolls rotting internal lint.
- **Management Strategy**:
  - Acid delinting of cotton seeds with commercial concentrated H2SO4 @ 100 ml/kg seed.
  - Spray Streptocycline @ 0.1 g/L (1 g/10 L) combined with Copper Oxychloride 50% WP @ 2.5 g/L. Repeat at 15-day intervals if rainfall continues.

header: B. Alternaria Leaf Spot (Alternaria macrospora)
content:
[B. Alternaria Leaf Spot (Alternaria macrospora)]
- **Symptoms**: Concentric circular to irregular brown spots with purple margins on leaves, primarily during boll development stage under humid cloudy weather.
- **Management**:
  - Spray Propiconazole 25% EC @ 1.0 ml/L or Pyraclostrobin 20% WG @ 1.0 g/L or Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5 g/L.

header: C. Grey Mildew / Dahiya Disease (Ramularia areola)
content:
[C. Grey Mildew / Dahiya Disease (Ramularia areola)]
- **Symptoms**: Angular pale translucent spots on the lower leaf surface covered with a powdery frost-white fungal growth. Leaves turn yellow, dry out, and shed prematurely.
- **Management**:
  - Foliar spray of Wettable Sulfur 80% WDG @ 3.0 g/L or Carbendazim 50% WP @ 1.0 g/L or Kresoxim-methyl 44.3% SC @ 1.0 ml/L.

header: D. Pink Bollworm (Pectinophora gossypiella)
content:
[D. Pink Bollworm (Pectinophora gossypiella)]
- **Symptoms**: Rosetted flowers (petals twisted into rosette), premature boll opening (locule damage), double seeds inside bolls, and staining of lint.
- **Management**:
  - Install delta/sleeve pheromone traps with Gossyplure @ 5 traps/acre for monitoring (economic threshold: 8 moths/trap/night for 3 consecutive days).
  - Release *Trichogramma bactrae* egg parasitoids @ 60,000/acre at weekly intervals.
  - For chemical knockdown: Spray Profenofos 50% EC @ 2.0 ml/L or Emamectin Benzoate 5% SG @ 0.4 g/L or Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC @ 0.3 ml/L.

header: 1. Overview & Agro-Ecological Zones
content:
[1. Overview & Agro-Ecological Zones]
- **Institutions**: ICAR - National Rice Research Institute (NRRI), Cuttack & University of Agricultural Sciences, Bengaluru / Mandya ZARS (V.C. Farm).
- **Major Karnataka Rice Ecosystems**: Cauvery Irrigation Basin (Mandya, Mysuru), Tunga-Bhadra Basin (Shivamogga, Ballari), Coastal Rainfed Lowlands (Udupi, Dakshina Kannada).
- **Varieties**: Jyothi, Jaya, IR-64, BPT-5204 (Samba Mahsuri), RNR-15048 (Telangana Sona / Low GI).

header: A. Rice Blast (Magnaporthe oryzae / Pyricularia oryzae)
content:
[A. Rice Blast (Magnaporthe oryzae / Pyricularia oryzae)]
- **Primary Source**: ICAR-NRRI Plant Pathology Compendium.
- **Symptoms**:
  - Leaf Blast: Spindle-shaped or eye-shaped lesions with grey/whitish centers and dark brown or reddish-brown borders. Spots coalesce causing extensive leaf drying (burn).
  - Neck Blast: Dark brown to black rot at the base of the panicle neck. Panicles break over, grains remain chaffy / empty (severest yield loss).
- **Cultural Practices**:
  - Avoid excessive nitrogenous fertilizer application (>120 kg N/ha in single splits). Split N in 3 doses (basal, tillering, panicle initiation).
- **Chemical Control (CIBRC Approved)**:
  - Prophylactic / Nursery: Tricyclazole 75% WP @ 0.6 g/L or Isoprothiolane 40% EC @ 1.5 ml/L.
  - Curative at Neck Blast stage: Azoxystrobin 18.2% + Difenoconazole 11.4% SC @ 1.0 ml/L or Trifloxystrobin 25% + Tebuconazole 50% WG @ 0.4 g/L.

header: B. Bacterial Leaf Blight (Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae)
content:
[B. Bacterial Leaf Blight (Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae)]
- **Symptoms**: Water-soaked stripes beginning at leaf tips and margins, expanding downward with characteristic wavy margins. Lesions turn straw-yellow to dirty white. In mornings, golden-yellow bacterial beads ooze from leaf margins.
- **Management**:
  - Drain standing water from the field for 2-3 days to lower canopy humidity.
  - Avoid top dressing nitrogen during disease flare-up.
  - Spray Copper Oxychloride 50% WP @ 2.5 g/L mixed with Streptocycline @ 0.1 g/L (1 g/10 L).

header: C. Sheath Blight (Rhizoctonia solani)
content:
[C. Sheath Blight (Rhizoctonia solani)]
- **Symptoms**: Oval or snake-skin like greenish-grey lesions with distinct brown irregular margins appearing on leaf sheaths near water level. Under high humidity, lesions spread upward into upper leaves and flag leaves.
- **Management**:
  - Spray Validamycin 3% L @ 2.0 ml/L or Hexaconazole 5% SC @ 2.0 ml/L or Thifluzamide 24% SC @ 0.75 ml/L at boot-leaf stage.

header: 1. Overview & Institution Source
content:
[1. Overview & Institution Source]
- **Primary Source**: ICAR - Indian Institute of Horticultural Research (IIHR), Hesaraghatta, Bengaluru.
- **Reference**: IIHR Horticultural Extension Bulletin No. 42 (Tomato Disease & Abiotic Health Diagnostics).

header: A. Blossom End Rot (Calcium Deficiency & Water Stress)
content:
[A. Blossom End Rot (Calcium Deficiency & Water Stress)]
- **Affected Plant Part**: Fruit (calyx end).
- **Symptoms**: Small, water-soaked, light brownish lesion on the blossom end (distal tip) of green fruit. The spot enlarges rapidly, flattens, and turns dark brown to black, leathery, and sunken.
- **Agronomic Cause**: Inadequate calcium transport during rapid cell division in young fruit, typically triggered by irregular soil moisture fluctuations or high electrical conductivity (EC).
- **Distinction from Anthracnose**: Blossom End Rot is strictly confined to the fruit apex/blossom scar, whereas Anthracnose produces concentric ring lesions across any shoulder surface of ripe fruit.
- **Management**:
  - Maintain regular, uniform drip irrigation; mulch beds to reduce soil moisture evaporation.
  - Foliar spray of Calcium Nitrate @ 4.0 - 5.0 g/L or Chelated Calcium (Ca-EDTA 10%) @ 1.0 g/L every 10 days starting at early fruit set.

header: B. Tomato Leaf Curl New Delhi Virus (ToLCNDV) & Whitefly Vector
content:
[B. Tomato Leaf Curl New Delhi Virus (ToLCNDV) & Whitefly Vector]
- **Affected Plant Part**: Canopy, young leaves, flower buds.
- **Symptoms**: Downward and upward curling of leaf margins, thick puckering, vein clearing, severe reduction in leaflet size (stunting), and bushy habit. Complete flower abortion if infected early.
- **Integrated Vector Management**:
  - Nursery protection under 40-mesh insect-proof netting for 25-30 days before field transplanting.
  - Erect 20-25 yellow sticky traps/acre at canopy level.
  - Foliar spray of Diafenthiuron 50% WP @ 1.2 g/L or Thiamethoxam 25% WG @ 0.3 g/L or Spiromesifen 22.9% SC @ 1.0 ml/L.

header: C. Tomato Pinworm / Leaf Miner (Tuta absoluta)
content:
[C. Tomato Pinworm / Leaf Miner (Tuta absoluta)]
- **Affected Plant Part**: Foliage, stems, green fruit.
- **Symptoms**: Transparent blister-like blotch mines in leaf parenchyma; pinhole entry punctures around fruit calyx leading to secondary rot.
- **Management**:
  - Install Tuta-specific pheromone lure traps @ 16-20 traps/acre.
  - Spray Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC @ 0.3 ml/L or Flubendiamide 39.35% SC @ 0.3 ml/L or Spinosad 45% SC @ 0.3 ml/L.

content:

header: A. Soil pH Spectrum in Karnataka Agricultural Zones
content:
[A. Soil pH Spectrum in Karnataka Agricultural Zones]
- **Acidic Soils (pH < 5.5)**: Prevalent in Western Ghats, Coastal Zone (Uttara Kannada, Udupi, Dakshina Kannada), and Malnad regions (Shivamogga, Chikkamagaluru, Kodagu).
  - *Nutrient Lockout*: Insoluble fixation of Phosphorus (P) with Aluminum/Iron oxides; Calcium (Ca) and Magnesium (Mg) base deficiency.
  - *Amelioration*: Apply Agricultural Dolomitic Lime @ 200 - 400 kg/acre every 3 years based on buffer pH test.
- **Neutral / Optimum Soils (pH 6.2 - 7.2)**: Southern Dry Zone (Mandya, Mysuru, Hassan, Tumakuru).
  - *Nutrient Bioavailability*: Maximum balanced availability of primary (N, P, K), secondary (S, Ca, Mg), and micronutrients.
- **Alkaline / Calcareous Soils (pH > 7.8, EC > 1.0 dS/m)**: Northern Dry Zone (Vijayapura, Bagalkote, Belagavi, Kalaburagi, Raichur).
  - *Nutrient Lockout*: Free Calcium Carbonate (CaCO3) fixes Phosphorus (P) as insoluble tricalcium phosphate; severe lockout of Iron (Fe), Zinc (Zn), and Manganese (Mn).
  - *Amelioration*: Application of Gypsum @ 500 kg/acre, green manuring with Sunnhemp / Dhaincha (Sesbania), and farmyard manure @ 4 tonnes/acre to generate organic carbonic acid.

header: 3. Plant Part Mobility Rules for Foliar Nutrient Diagnostics
content:
[3. Plant Part Mobility Rules for Foliar Nutrient Diagnostics]
- **Mobile Nutrients (N, P, K, Mg)**:
  - Mobilized from mature tissues to younger apical shoots under deficiency.
  - **Diagnostic Rule**: Deficiency symptoms appear **first on older, lower foliage**.
- **Immobile Nutrients (Fe, Zn, S, B, Ca, Cu, Mn)**:
  - Fixed inside cell walls and vascular lignin; cannot be translocated.
  - **Diagnostic Rule**: Deficiency symptoms appear **first on young, newly emerging leaves and terminal buds**.

header: A. Iron (Fe) Chlorosis Correction (Northern Calcareous Soils)
content:
[A. Iron (Fe) Chlorosis Correction (Northern Calcareous Soils)]
- **Foliar Spray**: Ferrous Sulfate (FeSO4) @ 5.0 g/L + Citric Acid @ 1.0 g/L (to prevent ferric precipitation). Spray twice at 10-day intervals.
- **Chelated Option**: Fe-EDTA (12% Fe) @ 1.0 - 1.5 g/L during active flush.

header: B. Zinc (Zn) Deficiency / Little Leaf Correction
content:
[B. Zinc (Zn) Deficiency / Little Leaf Correction]
- **Soil Basal Application**: Zinc Sulfate (ZnSO4 21%) @ 10 kg/acre before planting (valid for 2-3 crop cycles).
- **Foliar Spray**: Zinc Sulfate @ 2.5 g/L neutralized with 1.25 g/L slaked lime, or Zn-EDTA (12% Zn) @ 1.0 g/L.

header: C. General Balanced Recovery for Stress-Affected Crops
content:
[C. General Balanced Recovery for Stress-Affected Crops]
- **Foliar Spray**: Water-soluble 19:19:19 (NPK) @ 5.0 g/L mixed with multi-micronutrient mixture (Grade-1 Karnataka formulation) @ 2.5 ml/L.

header: 1. Overview & Agro-Climatic Requirements
content:
[1. Overview & Agro-Climatic Requirements]
- **Institution**: ICAR - Indian Institute of Maize Research (IIMR) & UAS Dharwad / Bengaluru.
- **Key Karnataka Hybrids**: Deccan 101, Deccan 103, Hema (NAH-1137), Nithyashree (NAH-2049), CP-818, Kargil 900M, Pioneer 3396.
- **Soil & pH**: Deep, well-drained fertile loam to silt loam soils rich in organic matter. Sensitive to water stagnation. Optimal pH: 6.0 to 7.5.
- **Climate & Temperature**: Warm-weather crop. Optimum germination temp 20°C - 24°C, growth temp 24°C - 32°C. Water requirement 500-650 mm.
- **Fertilizer Dose (Karnataka standard)**: 150:75:40 kg N:P2O5:K2O per hectare. 1/3rd N + full P & K as basal; 1/3rd N at knee-high stage (30 DAS); 1/3rd N at tasseling stage.

header: A. Common Rust (Puccinia sorghi)
content:
[A. Common Rust (Puccinia sorghi)]
- **Symptoms**: Small, powdery, circular to elongate golden-brown to cinnamon-brown pustules appearing on both upper and lower leaf surfaces. Later in the season, pustules turn brownish-black as teliospores form. Leaves turn chlorotic and desiccate prematurely under heavy infection.
- **Favorable Weather**: Cool temperatures (16°C - 24°C) with high relative humidity (>95%) and persistent morning dew, especially in late Kharif or Rabi plantings.
- **Management**:
  - Plant tolerant hybrids such as Hema or Deccan 103.
  - At first appearance of pustules: Spray Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5 g/L or Azoxystrobin 18.2% + Difenoconazole 11.4% SC @ 1.0 ml/L. Repeat after 15 days if rust pressure persists.

header: B. Turcicum Leaf Blight / Northern Leaf Blight (Exserohilum turcicum)
content:
[B. Turcicum Leaf Blight / Northern Leaf Blight (Exserohilum turcicum)]
- **Symptoms**: Long, elliptical, spindle-shaped greyish-green to tan lesions (2.5 to 15 cm long) with distinct margins. Under humid conditions, dark grey olivaceous spores cover lesions. Coalescing lesions cause extensive blighting ("fired" look).
- **Favorable Weather**: Moderate temperature (18°C - 27°C) accompanied by heavy dew and overcast rainy skies.
- **Management**:
  - Seed treatment: Metalaxyl + Mancozeb (Apron XL) @ 2 g/kg seed.
  - Foliar spray: Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5 g/L or Hexaconazole 5% EC @ 2 ml/L or Propiconazole 25% EC @ 1 ml/L at initiation of lower leaf lesions.

header: C. Fall Armyworm (FAW - Spodoptera frugiperda)
content:
[C. Fall Armyworm (FAW - Spodoptera frugiperda)]
- **Significance**: Major invasive destructive pest causing severe defoliation and ear damage across Karnataka maize tracts.
- **Symptoms**: Ragged leaf feeding holes, skeletonized whorl leaves filled with sawdust-like frass; central growing whorl chewed off ("dead heart").
- **Integrated Management**:
  - Deep summer ploughing to expose pupae to birds and sunlight.
  - Seed treatment with Cyantraniliprole 19.8% + Thiamethoxam 19.8% FS @ 6 ml/kg seed (protects crop for first 20 days).
  - Install FAW pheromone traps @ 5-6 traps/acre.
  - Early whorl application (15-25 DAS): Spray *Bacillus thuringiensis* (Bt) @ 2 g/L or *Metarhizium anisopliae* @ 5 g/L.
  - Chemical intervention (if >10% whorls infested): Spray Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC @ 0.4 ml/L or Spinetoram 11.7% SC @ 0.5 ml/L directed into leaf whorls.

header: 1. Overview & Agro-Climatic Requirements
content:
[1. Overview & Agro-Climatic Requirements]
- **Institution**: ICAR - National Rice Research Institute (NRRI) & University of Agricultural Sciences (UAS) Bengaluru & Dharwad.
- **Key Karnataka Varieties**:
  - Irrigated/Wetland: Jaya, Jyothi, MTU-1010, BPT-5204 (Samba Mahsuri), IR-64, KMP-101 (Thanu), BR-2655.
  - Rainfed/Upland: Dhiren, Sahbhagi Dhan, Intan.
- **Soil & pH**: Clayey to clay loam soils with high water holding capacity. Optimal pH: 5.5 to 7.0. Can tolerate moderate salinity up to EC 4.0 dS/m.
- **Climate & Rainfall**: Warm, humid climate. Optimum temperature 22°C to 32°C. Annual water requirement 1100-1400 mm.
- **Fertilizer Recommendation (NPK for Karnataka)**:
  - High yielding varieties: 100:50:50 kg N:P2O5:K2O per hectare.
  - Split application of Nitrogen: 50% at basal, 25% at tillering (20-25 DAT), 25% at panicle initiation. Apply Zinc Sulphate @ 25 kg/ha basal.

header: A. Rice Blast (Magnaporthe oryzae / Pyricularia oryzae)
content:
[A. Rice Blast (Magnaporthe oryzae / Pyricularia oryzae)]
- **Symptoms**:
  - Leaf Blast: Spindle-shaped or eye-shaped spots with grey or whitish centers and brown/reddish margins. Spots enlarge and coalesce, causing entire leaves to wither and dry.
  - Neck Blast: Brown to black lesion encircling the panicle base/neck node; panicles break and hang down, producing chaffy unfilled grains.
- **Favorable Weather**: Relative humidity >90%, dew formation, night temperatures between 18°C - 24°C, excess nitrogenous fertilization.
- **Cultural Practices**:
  - Avoid excessive nitrogen fertilizer. Split nitrogen into 3-4 doses.
  - Treat seeds before sowing with Tricyclazole 75% WP @ 2 g/kg or *Pseudomonas fluorescens* @ 10 g/kg seed.
- **Chemical Control**:
  - Spray Tricyclazole 75% WP (Beam) @ 0.6 g/L water, or Isoprothiolane 40% EC @ 1.5 ml/L, or Kasugamycin 3% SL @ 2.5 ml/L.
  - In severe neck blast risk areas, apply preventive spray at heading stage.

header: B. Bacterial Leaf Blight (BLB - Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae)
content:
[B. Bacterial Leaf Blight (BLB - Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae)]
- **Symptoms**: Water-soaked stripes starting from leaf tips and margins, expanding into wavy, yellowish-white lesions running parallel to veins. Tiny amber droplets of bacterial ooze appear on young lesions in early morning. "Kresek" (seedling wilt) stage causes complete seedling drying.
- **Favorable Weather**: Heavy rainfall, strong winds during monsoon, high humidity, water stagnation.
- **Management**:
  - Drain excess field water temporarily.
  - Avoid top dressing nitrogen during disease flare-up; apply additional Muriate of Potash (MOP) @ 25 kg/ha to improve plant immunity.
  - Spray Copper Hydroxide 53.8% DF @ 2.0 g/L or Copper Oxychloride 50% WP @ 2.5 g/L mixed with Streptocycline @ 0.1 g/L (1 g in 10 L water).

header: C. Rice Sheath Blight (Rhizoctonia solani)
content:
[C. Rice Sheath Blight (Rhizoctonia solani)]
- **Symptoms**: Oval or irregular greenish-grey water-soaked spots on leaf sheaths near water line. Spots enlarge with dark brown boundaries and greyish white center ("snake skin" pattern). Lesions spread up to flag leaf.
- **Management**:
  - Deep summer ploughing and destruction of infected stubble.
  - Foliar spray of Hexaconazole 5% SC @ 2.0 ml/L or Validamycin 3% L @ 2.0 ml/L or Propiconazole 25% EC (Tilt) @ 1.0 ml/L.

header: D. Brown Plant Hopper (BPH - Nilaparvata lugens)
content:
[D. Brown Plant Hopper (BPH - Nilaparvata lugens)]
- **Symptoms**: Both nymphs and adults suck sap from leaf sheath bases. Plants turn yellow, dry up rapidly and lodge in circular patches known as "Hopper Burn".
- **Management**:
  - Provide "Alley ways" (skip one row after every 8-10 rows) for light penetration and air movement.
  - Alternate wetting and drying (AWD) water management.
  - Spray Pymetrozine 50% WG @ 0.6 g/L or Triflumezopyrim 10% SC @ 0.48 ml/L or Dinotefuran 20% SG @ 0.4 g/L directed at stem bases.

header: 1. Overview & Agro-Climatic Requirements
content:
[1. Overview & Agro-Climatic Requirements]
- **Institution**: University of Agricultural Sciences (UAS), Bengaluru & Mandya/Mysuru Dry Farming Stations.
- **Key Karnataka Varieties**:
  - High Yielding & Blast Resistant: GPU-28, ML-365 (drought tolerant, blast resistant), KMR-301, GPU-48, Indaf-8, Indaf-9, MR-1, MR-6.
- **Soil & Climate**:
  - Red loamy, sandy loam, lateritic soils with good internal drainage.
  - Soil pH: 5.5 to 7.5.
  - Temperature: 22°C to 30°C. Thrives under 600-900 mm rainfall, highly drought hardy with C4 carbon fixation pathway.
- **Sowing Window**:
  - Kharif rainfed: July 1st to July 25th.
  - Late Kharif: up to August 15th (using short duration varieties like GPU-48 or ML-365).
  - Seed rate: Drilling/Broadcasting 10-12 kg/ha; Transplanting 5 kg/ha.

header: A. Ragi Blast (Pyricularia grisea)
content:
[A. Ragi Blast (Pyricularia grisea)]
- **Significance**: Most destructive disease of finger millet in Karnataka, affecting leaf, neck, and finger stages.
- **Symptoms**:
  - Leaf Blast: Diamond/spindle shaped lesions with grey ash center and reddish-brown borders on seedlings and leaves.
  - Neck Blast: Inverted dark brown to black ring at the junction below earhead panicle; earhead turns premature white and lodges.
  - Finger Blast: Dark brown infection on individual fingers of earhead, inhibiting grain filling and leading to shrivelled grains.
- **Favorable Weather**: Continuous cloudy weather, drizzle, high relative humidity (>85%), temperatures between 20°C - 26°C.
- **Cultural & Preventive**:
  - Cultivate resistant cultivars: GPU-28, ML-365, or KMR-301.
  - Seed Treatment: Treat seeds with Carbendazim 50% WP @ 2.0 g/kg or *Pseudomonas fluorescens* @ 10 g/kg seed before sowing.
- **Chemical Control**:
  - At first appearance of leaf blast: Spray Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.0 g/L or Tricyclazole 75% WP @ 0.6 g/L.
  - Protect earhead (neck/finger blast): Crucial single spray at 50% earhead emergence with Kitazin (IBP) 48% EC @ 1.0 ml/L or Tricyclazole 75% WP @ 0.6 g/L.

header: B. Foot Rot / Seedling Blight (Sclerotium rolfsii / Helminthosporium nodulosum)
content:
[B. Foot Rot / Seedling Blight (Sclerotium rolfsii / Helminthosporium nodulosum)]
- **Symptoms**: Brown lesions on basal sheath near soil line, rotting of seedlings, white cottony mycelium at collar region, damping-off patches in nursery.
- **Management**:
  - Seed treatment with *Trichoderma harzianum* @ 5 g/kg seed.
  - Soil solarization and avoid waterlogging. Drench soil patch with Carbendazim 50% WP @ 1 g/L or Copper Oxychloride @ 2.5 g/L.

header: C. Major Pests of Ragi
content:
[C. Major Pests of Ragi]
- **Ragi Stem Borer (Sesamia inferens)**: Larvae bore into central shoot causing "dead heart" in vegetative phase and white earhead in flowering stage.
  - Control: Apply Cartap Hydrochloride 4G granules @ 8 kg/acre or spray Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC @ 0.3 ml/L.
- **Ragi Earhead Caterpillar**: Caterpillars feed on milk-stage grain within earheads.
  - Control: Dust Quinalphos 1.5% DP @ 10 kg/acre or spray Novaluron 10% EC @ 1.0 ml/L at grain formation.

header: 1. Overview & Agro-Climatic Requirements
content:
[1. Overview & Agro-Climatic Requirements]
- **Institution**: ICAR - Indian Institute of Horticultural Research (IIHR), Bengaluru & UAS Bengaluru / Raitha Mitra.
- **Recommended Varieties & Hybrids**: Arka Rakshak (triple disease resistant to ToLCV, BW, Early Blight), Arka Samrat, Arka Vikas, Arka Abhed.
- **Optimal Soil**: Well-drained sandy loam or clay loam, rich in organic matter.
- **Soil pH**: 6.0 to 7.0. EC < 1.0 dS/m.
- **Temperature & Climate**: 21°C to 28°C during vegetative stage; daytime 24°C-30°C, nighttime 16°C-20°C for fruit set. Extreme heat (>35°C) causes flower drop.
- **Water Management**: Drip irrigation recommended; water requirement 400-600 mm throughout crop lifecycle. Avoid wetting foliage during flowering/fruiting to prevent fungal foliar blights.

header: A. Tomato Early Blight (Alternaria solani)
content:
[A. Tomato Early Blight (Alternaria solani)]
- **Symptoms**: Concentric brown-to-black ring spots ("target board" pattern) appearing first on older lower leaves. Leaves turn yellow around spots, dry out, and drop prematurely (defoliation).
- **Favorable Weather**: Warm temperatures (24°C - 30°C) with intermittent rain and high relative humidity (>80%).
- **Cultural & Preventive**:
  - Maintain 60 cm x 45 cm or 90 cm x 60 cm spacing for aeration.
  - Stake plants with bamboo poles to prevent leaves touching wet soil.
  - Remove and burn infected lower leaves up to 30 cm from ground.
- **Organic & Biological Control**:
  - Spray *Pseudomonas fluorescens* or *Bacillus subtilis* @ 5 g/L or 10 ml/L at transplanting and 30 DAT.
  - Foliar spray of 5% Neem Seed Kernel Extract (NSKE) or Cold-pressed Neem Oil (10,000 ppm) @ 3 ml/L.
- **Chemical Control (CIBRC Approved Dosages)**:
  - Preventive / Initial symptoms: Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.0 - 2.5 g/L or Chlorothalonil 75% WP @ 2.0 g/L.
  - Curative / Severe infection: Azoxystrobin 18.2% + Difenoconazole 11.4% SC @ 1.0 ml/L, or Tebuconazole 25.9% EC @ 1.0 ml/L.
  - Spray volume: 500 L/ha. Wait period (PHI): 5-7 days before harvest.

header: B. Tomato Late Blight (Phytophthora infestans)
content:
[B. Tomato Late Blight (Phytophthora infestans)]
- **Symptoms**: Water-soaked dark green/black lesions on leaf margins and tips. Under moist morning conditions, white downy fungal mildew appears on leaf undersides. Stems show purplish-brown lesions; fruits develop large, greasy brown firm lesions.
- **Favorable Weather**: Cool temperatures (13°C - 21°C) with prolonged cloud cover, fog, and relative humidity >90%.
- **Cultural Practices**:
  - Avoid night irrigation and overhead sprinklers. Ensure ridge planting with proper soil drainage.
- **Chemical Control**:
  - Prophylactic: Copper Oxychloride 50% WP @ 2.5 g/L or Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5 g/L.
  - Systemic curative: Metalaxyl 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP (Ridomil Gold) @ 2.5 g/L, or Cymoxanil 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP @ 2.0 g/L, or Dimethomorph 50% WP @ 1.0 g/L.

header: C. Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus (ToLCV) & Whitefly Vector
content:
[C. Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus (ToLCV) & Whitefly Vector]
- **Symptoms**: Severe stunting, upward curling and cupping of leaflets, marginal chlorosis (yellowing), puckering, and bushy appearance. Flowers fail to develop; severe yield loss if infected before flowering.
- **Vector**: Bemisia tabaci (Silverleaf Whitefly).
- **Management Strategy**:
  - Grow resistant hybrids like Arka Rakshak or Arka Abhed.
  - Use 40-mesh nylon insect-proof net in nursery beds for first 25-30 days.
  - Install yellow sticky traps @ 20-25 traps per acre at 1 foot above canopy level.
  - Vector control: Spray Imidacloprid 17.8% SL @ 0.5 ml/L or Thiamethoxam 25% WG @ 0.3 g/L or Acetamiprid 20% SP @ 0.4 g/L. Alternate with neem oil 3 ml/L to prevent pesticide resistance.

header: D. Bacterial Wilt (Ralstonia solanacearum)
content:
[D. Bacterial Wilt (Ralstonia solanacearum)]
- **Symptoms**: Rapid daytime wilting of plant while foliage retains green color (green wilt). Stem cross-section placed in water emits white bacterial ooze streams.
- **Management**:
  - Soil solarization in nursery. Apply bleaching powder @ 10 kg/acre before planting.
  - Crop rotation with non-solanaceous crops (maize, ragi, pulses) for 2-3 years.
  - Drench root zone with Copper Hydroxide 77% WP @ 2.0 g/L + Streptocycline (Streptomycin sulphate + Tetracycline) @ 0.1 g/L (1 g in 10 L water).

header: E. Tomato Fruit Borer (Helicoverpa armigera)
content:
[E. Tomato Fruit Borer (Helicoverpa armigera)]
- **Symptoms**: Circular bore holes on green and ripe fruits, often with caterpillar half inside fruit.
- **Management**:
  - Plant African Marigold as trap crop (1 row of marigold for every 16 rows of tomato).
  - Install Helilure pheromone traps @ 5-8 traps/acre.
  - Spray HaNPV @ 250 LE/ha or Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) @ 2 g/L.
  - Chemical spray: Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC (Coragen) @ 0.3 ml/L or Flubendiamide 39.35% SC @ 0.3 ml/L. PHI: 3 days.

header: 1. Primary Sources & Research Institutions
content:
[1. Primary Sources & Research Institutions]
- **Institutions**:
  - ICAR - Central Plantation Crops Research Institute (CPCRI), Kasaragod & Regional Station, Vittal (Karnataka).
  - ICAR - Central Citrus Research Institute (CCRI), Nagpur.
  - University of Horticultural Sciences (UHS), Bagalkote.

header: A. Coconut Stem Bleeding (Thielaviopsis paradoxa / Ceratocystis paradoxa)
content:
[A. Coconut Stem Bleeding (Thielaviopsis paradoxa / Ceratocystis paradoxa)]
- **Primary Source**: ICAR-CPCRI Technical Bulletin No. 58 (Coconut Disease Management).
- **Affected Plant Part**: Trunk, Bark, Stem lower column.
- **Symptoms**:
  - Dark brown or reddish-brown liquid exudes from longitudinal cracks on the stem bark, typically within 2-3 meters from ground level.
  - The exuded sap dries into a dark, viscous, tarry patch. Internal stem tissue rots into a fibrous brown mass.
- **Integrated Management**:
  - Chisel out affected decayed fibrous bark and wood tissue cleanly until healthy tissue is reached.
  - Swab the wound with Coal Tar or Bordeaux Paste (1 kg Copper Sulfate + 1 kg Slaked Lime in 10 L water).
  - Apply 5 kg neem cake per palm around the basin.
  - Root feeding: In severe cases, root-feed with Hexaconazole 5% SC @ 2 ml in 100 ml water per palm.

header: B. Coconut Bud Rot (Phytophthora palmivora)
content:
[B. Coconut Bud Rot (Phytophthora palmivora)]
- **Affected Plant Part**: Crown, spindle leaf, apical bud.
- **Symptoms**: Yellowing and withered drooping of the central spindle leaf. The central spear leaf rots easily when pulled, emitting a foul odor.
- **Management**:
  - Cut away rotted heart tissues cleanly. Place 2 sachets of Mancozeb 75% WP (5 g each wrapped in perforated cloth) into the leaf axils of the crown.
  - Prophylactic spraying: Spray Bordeaux Mixture 1% on the crown before the onset of monsoon rains.

header: A. Citrus Canker (Xanthomonas citri subsp. citri)
content:
[A. Citrus Canker (Xanthomonas citri subsp. citri)]
- **Primary Source**: ICAR-CCRI Disease Advisory Bulletin.
- **Affected Plant Part**: Leaf, Twig, Stem, Fruit peel.
- **Symptoms**:
  - Leaves: Raised, blister-like corky lesions with crater-like centers, surrounded by a distinct oily or yellow halo.
  - Stems/Twigs: Rough, brown corky eruptions causing twig dieback.
  - Fruits: Dark, rough, cratered scabby eruptions on the rind. Internal fruit flesh is unaffected but unmarketable.
- **Management**:
  - Prune and burn infected twigs before monsoon.
  - Spray Streptocycline @ 0.1 g/L (1 g/10 L) mixed with Copper Oxychloride 50% WP @ 2.5 g/L at 20-day intervals during new vegetative flushes.

header: B. Citrus Greening / Huanglongbing (Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus)
content:
[B. Citrus Greening / Huanglongbing (Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus)]
- **Affected Plant Part**: Whole Canopy, Foliage, Fruit.
- **Symptoms**: Asymmetric blotchy mottle chlorosis across leaf veins (veins do not remain neatly green as in iron deficiency). Upright, small leaves. Fruits remain small, lopsided, poorly colored with bitter juice.
- **Vector Control**: Diaphorina citri (Asian Citrus Psyllid). Spray Imidacloprid 17.8% SL @ 0.5 ml/L or Thiamethoxam 25% WG @ 0.3 g/L during active leaf flush.
